examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A matching is a set of vertex-disjoint edges; a maximal matching cannot be enlarged locally, whereas a maximum matching has largest cardinality globally. To count path matchings, condition on whether an endpoint is matched. For bipartite graphs, Hall’s condition characterizes a matching covering the left side; König’s theorem equates maximum matching and minimum vertex-cover sizes.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
How many matchings, including the empty matching, does a path on 6 vertices have?

**Answer: 13.** Let M(n)=M(n−1)+M(n−2), according as the first vertex is unmatched or matched to its neighbour. M(0)=M(1)=1, so M(2)=2,M(3)=3,M(4)=5,M(5)=8,M(6)=13.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A maximum matching need not be perfect. A vertex cover and an edge cover cover different objects and obey different counting results.

A maximal matching may be smaller than a maximum matching.
